lines: Impulse generator: a burst of coloured noise shaped by a window function, started by a gate and repeated for as long as that gate is high
Picks the colour of the noise in the burst: white, pink, red, violet, grey, blue or black
Picks the window function that shapes the burst: none, triangle, Welch, sine, Hanning, Blackman, Nutall or Kaiser, with its name printed under the display
Sets how long one burst lasts, 0.1ms to 100ms
Sets how many peaks the window is folded into within one burst, 1 to 4
Sets how long after one burst begins the next one begins while the gate is high, 1ms to 1000ms
Adds to the noise colour, 10V stepping from white through to black
Adds to the window function, 10V stepping across all eight
Adds to the burst length, 10V covering the whole 0.1ms to 100ms range
Adds to the peak count, 10V covering 1 to 4 peaks
Adds to the repeat time, 10V covering the whole 1ms to 1000ms range
A rising edge here starts a burst, and while this is above 0V the burst starts again at the repeat time
The noise burst
Note — nothing comes out until a gate or a trigger is patched into the gate input; there is no free-running mode, and the output rests at 0V between bursts
Stereo filter morphed through a cube: each corner of the cube holds the settings of up to seven filters, and the three axis knobs move between the corners
Picks which cube of filter settings is used, numbered from zero through the cubes in the loaded file
Moves the first channel along the frequency axis of the cube, 0 to 100% on a logarithmic scale
Moves the first channel along the Y axis of the cube, 0 to 100%
Moves the first channel along the Z axis of the cube, 0 to 100%
Moves the second channel along the frequency axis of the cube, 0 to 100% on a logarithmic scale, and LINK replaces this setting with the first channel one
Moves the second channel along the Y axis of the cube, 0 to 100%, and LINK replaces this setting with the first channel one
Moves the second channel along the Z axis of the cube, 0 to 100%, and LINK replaces this setting with the first channel one
Makes the second channel use the first row of FREQUENCY, Y and Z in place of the second row, so both channels are filtered alike
Turns the two inputs into their sum and their difference before filtering and back into left and right after, so the first row filters the middle and the second the sides
The left channel into the filter, or the middle of the stereo image when MID-SIDE is on
The right channel into the filter, or the sides of the stereo image when MID-SIDE is on; nothing is normalled here, so it reads 0V unpatched
Adds to the model number, 10V covering every cube in the loaded file
Adds to the first channel's position on the frequency axis, 10V covering the whole axis
Adds to the first channel's position on the Y axis, 10V covering the whole axis
Adds to the first channel's position on the Z axis, 10V covering the whole axis
Adds to the second channel's position on the frequency axis, 10V covering the whole axis
Adds to the second channel's position on the Y axis, 10V covering the whole axis
Adds to the second channel's position on the Z axis, 10V covering the whole axis
The filtered left channel, clamped to ±10V
The filtered right channel, clamped to ±10V
Note — a default set of filter cubes ships with the plugin and is read in as soon as the module is placed, so no file has to be chosen before it will work
Menu — Load Model Cube File — replaces the filter cubes with a set read from a JSON file of your own; the plugin folder holds the default file and a note on writing one
Banded waveguide oscillator: an impulse is split into three bands, two of them ringing in short delay lines and the top one in a waveguide mesh
Picks the shape of the mesh: rectilinear, triangular or cubic
Sets how many junctions the mesh has along each dimension, 2 to 5; the larger sizes cost a great deal more processing for little change in sound
Multiplies the input plus the fed-back output by 1 to 5 before it is hard-limited, which distorts the excitation as it is driven
Sets the centre frequency of the band that feeds the first waveguide delay, 60Hz to 10000Hz
Sets the centre frequency of the band that feeds the second waveguide delay, 60Hz to 10000Hz, forced above the first band
Sets the centre frequency of the band that feeds the mesh, 60Hz to 10000Hz, forced above the second band
Sets the length of the first waveguide delay, 1 to 500 samples
Sets the length of the second waveguide delay, 1 to 500 samples
Sets the delay along each link between mesh junctions, 2 to 1000 samples
Sets how much of the signal reaching an edge of the mesh is reflected back inverted, 0 to 95%
Multiplies the signal at each edge of the mesh by 1 to 5 before it is hard-limited and reflected
Sets how much of the output is added back to the input, 0 to 100%
The impulse that excites the waveguides and the mesh, 5V being full scale
Adds to the mesh size, 10V covering 2 to 5 junctions
Adds to the non-linearity of the excitation, 10V covering 1 to 5
Adds to the first band's centre frequency, 10V covering the whole range
Adds to the second band's centre frequency, 10V covering the whole range
Adds to the mesh band's centre frequency, 10V covering the whole range
Adds to the first waveguide delay, 10V covering 1 to 500 samples
Adds to the second waveguide delay, 10V covering 1 to 500 samples
Adds to the mesh link delay, 10V covering the whole range
Adds to the mesh edge reflection, 10V covering 0 to 95%
Adds to the mesh edge non-linearity, 10V covering 1 to 5
Adds to the feedback amount, 10V covering 0 to 100%
The two waveguide delays and one junction of the mesh added together
Note — there is no exciter inside this module; the waveguides and the mesh ring only while something is patched into the impulse input, and with that jack empty the output stays at 0V
DanceThisMeshAround.notes: Four parameters and four inputs are declared with no widget on the panel (mesh impedance, the two waveguide feedback CVs and an allpass cutoff CV), so they can never be clicked and are left untagged. The second output is declared and never drawn.

lines: Spectral vocoder: two inputs are analysed into 1024 frequency bands and each band of one is multiplied by a band of the other, with the pairing and the stereo placement drawn on the grids
The first signal into the vocoder, whose bands are paired with bands of the second
The second signal into the vocoder, whose bands are paired with bands of the first
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the BAND SHIFT grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the BAND SHIFT drawing up and down the frequency bands, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Scales every value on the BAND SHIFT grid by the cosine of this angle about the pin, 0 to 180 degrees either way, so half a turn flattens the drawing onto the pin and a whole turn mirrors it
Adds to the rotation of the BAND SHIFT grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Sets where the pin lies across the range of the BAND SHIFT grid, 0 to 100%
Adds to the pin position on the BAND SHIFT grid, 10V covering the whole range
Cycles the pin mode for the BAND SHIFT grid: off, hold values below the pin up to it, leave values below the pin alone, hold values above the pin down to it, or leave values above the pin alone
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the PANNING grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the PANNING drawing up and down the frequency bands, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Scales every value on the PANNING grid by the cosine of this angle about the pin, 0 to 180 degrees either way, so half a turn flattens the drawing onto the pin and a whole turn mirrors it
Adds to the rotation of the PANNING grid, 5V being 180 degrees
Sets where the pin lies across the range of the PANNING grid, 0 to 100%
Adds to the pin position on the PANNING grid, 10V covering the whole range
Cycles the pin mode for the PANNING grid: off, hold values below the pin up to it, leave values below the pin alone, hold values above the pin down to it, or leave values above the pin alone
Multiplies the BAND SHIFT drawing into a number of bands, -1024 to 1024, so a full-height bar moves that band of the second input that far before it is paired
Adds to the band spread, 10V covering the whole -1024 to 1024 range
Turns inversion on for the first input: every band louder than the threshold is replaced by the loudest band's level minus its own
Turns inversion on for the second input: every band louder than the threshold is replaced by the loudest band's level minus its own
Sets how loud a band of the first input must be before inversion changes it, 0 to 50; at 0 every band is inverted and the sound becomes very noisy
Adds to the inversion threshold of the first input, 10V covering 0 to 50
Sets how loud a band of the second input must be before inversion changes it, 0 to 50; at 0 every band is inverted and the sound becomes very noisy
Adds to the inversion threshold of the second input, 10V covering 0 to 50
The left channel of the vocoded result, where a band the PANNING grid moves left is up to twice as loud and one moved fully right is silent
The right channel of the vocoded result, where a band the PANNING grid moves right is up to twice as loud; moving a band left does not quieten it here
Note — each band of the first input is multiplied by a band of the second, so both inputs have to be patched; with one of them empty the outputs stay silent
Note — a grid is drawn on by dragging across it, and holding shift while dragging keeps the drag on the band it started on, so one band can be set without disturbing its neighbours
Note — each grid is one display rather than one control per band, so no band can be clicked for a line of its own
Note — right-clicking a grid opens that grid's own menu rather than the module's, and All Maximum, All Minimum, All Half, Triangle, Sine, Ramp and Random fill the grid with that shape
Note — a grid's own right-click menu also carries Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Reduce By Half, Shift Left and Shift Right, which rework what is already drawn on it
Menu — # of Frequency Bands — sets the analysis to 1024, 2048 or 4096 bands
Menu — Window Function — picks the shape each frame is multiplied by before analysis: None, Triangle, Welch, Sine, Hanning, Blackman, Nutall or Kaiser
Morphology.notes: The frame size parameter and a third output are declared with no widget on the panel, so they can never be clicked and are left untagged.

DelayedReaction.notes: The maker configures the left output twice and the right output not at all, so Rack shows the tooltip "Right" on the left jack and no name on the right one; the code writes the left channel to the first jack and the right channel to the second. The frame size parameter has no widget on the panel. The panning read at the output is indexed by overlapping frame rather than by frequency band, so only the four lowest bands of the PANNING grid reach the output at all.

lines: Wavetable oscillator whose tables are spread over a sphere: turning the sphere brings different tables to the point being played, and the four nearest are morphed together
Sets the pitch, -54 to 54 semitones from C4 at 261.63Hz
Adds to the pitch at one volt per octave, and its channel count sets the polyphony of the whole oscillator
Turns the sphere about its yaw axis, -100% to 100%, bringing different wavetables to the point being played
Adds to the yaw rotation, 10V covering the whole turn
Turns the sphere about its pitch axis, -100% to 100%, bringing different wavetables to the point being played
Adds to the pitch-axis rotation, 10V covering the whole turn
Turns the sphere about its roll axis, -100% to 100%, bringing different wavetables to the point being played
Adds to the roll rotation, 10V covering the whole turn
Cycles how the four nearest wavetables are combined: interpolated by distance, their spectra averaged, their spectra averaged ignoring phase, or three of them used as a transfer function on the first
Attenuates the FM input before it is added to the pitch, 0 to 100%
Adds to the FM amount, 10V covering 0 to 100%
Modulates the pitch through the FM AMT knob, at a volt per octave when that knob is full; polyphonic
Sets the phase the wave is read from, 0-5V covering the whole cycle
Syncs the oscillator as the SYNC TYPE button is set, acting on the upward zero crossings; patching anything here turns syncing on
Cycles what a sync does: hard restarts the wave at every zero crossing, soft restarts it only when the phase is before the sync position, and soft reverse runs the wave backwards from there instead
Sets the phase a soft sync acts before, 0 to 100% of the cycle, drawn as the gold line
Adds to the sync position, 10V covering the whole cycle
Shifts which values of the four wavetables are combined in the interpolate and transfer modes, and which frequency bands are combined in the spectral modes, -64 to 64 steps
Adds to the spectrum shift, 10V covering -64 to 64 steps
Sets how hard the output wave is folded back on itself, 1 to 4
Adds to the fold amount, 10V covering 1 to 4
Chooses what happens to the part of the wave past the fold: it is turned back on itself, or decimated
Adds an offset to every level drawn on the HARMONICS grid, 5V covering the whole range; the grid acts in the two spectral morph modes
Slides the HARMONICS drawing across the first sixteen harmonics, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
The oscillator, ±5V, with as many channels as the V/Oct input
Note — the sphere is empty when the module is placed and the outputs stay at 0V; a wavetable has to be read in with Load WaveTable, Add WaveTable or Load Directory first
Note — the harmonic grid is drawn on by dragging across it, and holding shift while dragging keeps the drag on the harmonic it started on
Note — the harmonic grid is one display rather than one control per harmonic, so no harmonic can be clicked for a line of its own
Note — right-clicking the harmonic grid opens that grid's own menu rather than the module's: All Maximum, All Minimum, All Half, Triangle, Sine, Ramp and Random fill it with that shape
Note — the harmonic grid's own right-click menu also carries Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Reduce By Half, Shift Up and Shift Down, which rework what is already drawn on it
Menu — Load WaveTable — replaces the sphere with the tables of one Serum-style wavetable file, read as 2048 points per table
Menu — Add WaveTable — reads another wavetable file onto the sphere alongside the tables already there
Menu — Load Directory — reads every wavetable file in a folder onto the sphere
Menu — Sample Scatter — a slider, 0 to 100%, moving tables that came from the same file further apart on the sphere
BallOfConfusion.notes: Three quantize parameters and two outputs are declared with no widget on the panel, so they can never be clicked and are left untagged.

lines: Resynthesiser: one or two incoming signals are analysed into frequency bands, and up to 36 oscillators are driven from the strongest of those bands
The first signal to be analysed and resynthesised
The second signal to be analysed, which the MORPHING grid blends against the first
Sets how many oscillators are driven, 1 to 36
Adds to the voice count, 10V covering 1 to 36 oscillators
Picks the waveform every oscillator uses: sine, triangle, sawtooth, square or a rectangle a quarter of a cycle wide
Adds to the waveform, 10V stepping across all five
Scales the frequency of every oscillator, doubling it at +1 and quadrupling it at +3, halving it at -1.5 and falling to 20Hz at -3, which is not the octave scaling the tooltip names
Adds to the frequency scaling, 10V covering the whole -3 to 3 range
Sets how far each oscillator is pushed away from the warp centre frequency, 0 to 100%, which at 100% doubles its distance from that centre
Adds to the warp amount, 10V covering 0 to 100%
Sets the frequency the warp pushes the oscillators away from, 0Hz to 10000Hz
Adds to the warp centre frequency, 10V covering 0Hz to 10000Hz
Adds the frequency of the first voice to the warp centre, so the centre follows the analysed fundamental and CENTER becomes an offset from it
Sets the middle of the part of the spectrum searched for the strongest bands, 0 to 100%
Adds to the analysis centre, 10V covering the whole spectrum
Sets how wide a part of the spectrum is searched for the strongest bands, 0 to 100%, where 100% reaches everything
Adds to the analysis bandwidth, 10V covering 0 to 100%
Picks how the strongest bands are handed to the oscillators: normal, inverted magnitude, reverse, or reverse with inverted magnitude
Adds to the spectral mode, 10V stepping across all four

Adds to the voice shift, 10V covering -35 to 35 voices
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the FM MATRIX grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the FM MATRIX drawing across the oscillators, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds an offset to every value on the FM AMOUNT grid, 0 to 100% of its range
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the FM AMOUNT grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the FM AMOUNT drawing across the oscillators, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
A frequency modulation source for whichever oscillators the FM MATRIX assigns to it; polyphonic, and 5V shifts an oscillator by 10000Hz
A second frequency modulation source for whichever oscillators the FM MATRIX assigns to it; polyphonic, and 5V shifts an oscillator by 10000Hz
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the AM/RM MATRIX grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the AM/RM MATRIX drawing across the oscillators, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds an offset to every value on the AM/RM MIX grid, 0 to 100% of its range
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the AM/RM MIX grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the AM/RM MIX drawing across the oscillators, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
A modulator for whichever oscillators the AM/RM MATRIX assigns to it; polyphonic
A second modulator for whichever oscillators the AM/RM MATRIX assigns to it; polyphonic
Makes the AM/RM matrix ring-modulate the oscillators against one another rather than against the AM/RM inputs, and turns the mix grid into a blend between an oscillator and that ring modulation
Adds an offset to every value on the MORPHING grid, -100% to 100% of its range, moving every oscillator between the first input and the second
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the MORPHING grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the MORPHING drawing across the oscillators, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Adds an offset to every value drawn on the PANNING grid, 5V covering the whole range
Slides the PANNING drawing across the oscillators, 5V covering the whole height of the grid
Sets how much of the output is added back into both analysis inputs, 0 to 100%
Adds to the feedback, 10V covering 0 to 100%
Sets the balance between the two inputs added together and the resynthesis, 0 to 100% resynthesised
Adds to the mix, 10V covering dry to fully resynthesised
The left channel of the result, carrying the whole unpanned mix while the right output is unpatched
The right channel of the result
Note — a grid is drawn on by dragging across it, and holding shift while dragging keeps the drag on the band it started on, so one band can be set without disturbing its neighbours
Note — each grid is one display rather than one control per band, so no band can be clicked for a line of its own
Note — right-clicking a grid opens that grid's own menu rather than the module's, and All Maximum, All Minimum, All Half, Triangle, Sine, Ramp and Random fill the grid with that shape
Note — a grid's own right-click menu also carries Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Reduce By Half, Shift Left and Shift Right, which rework what is already drawn on it
Menu — # of Frequency Bands for In 1 — sets the analysis of the first input to 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048 or 4096 bands; small frames follow transients, large ones read pitch better
Menu — # of Frequency Bands for In 2 — sets the analysis of the second input to 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048 or 4096 bands; small frames follow transients, large ones read pitch better

HarmonicConvergence.notes: The FEEDBACK knob is drawn on the panel but never named in the code, so Rack shows it with no tooltip; it scales the output fed back into both analysis inputs. The FREQ. SHIFT knob is named in octaves and documented as ±3 octaves, but the code multiplies the analysed frequency by 1 plus the setting going up and by 1 plus a third of it going down.

FreudianSlip.notes: The TUNING input is named V/Oct by the maker but is read like every other CV on the plugin: it adds a tenth of its voltage times the parameter range, so one volt adds 0.6 to a -3 to 3 setting. lines: Granular synthesiser with 16 sample slots and 16 incoming-signal voices: grains are spawned from whichever of the 32 voices the weighting picks, each with its own size, pitch, envelope and position

Note — a grain is only ever taken from a slot that holds a sample or from a patched input jack, so read a file in with Load Sample 1 or Load Directory before expecting sound
Note — a grid is drawn on by dragging across it, and holding shift while dragging keeps the drag on the band it started on, so one band can be set without disturbing its neighbours
Note — each grid is one display rather than one control per band, so no band can be clicked for a line of its own
Note — right-clicking a grid opens that grid's own menu rather than the module's, and All Maximum, All Minimum, All Half, Triangle, Sine, Ramp and Random fill the grid with that shape
Note — a grid's own right-click menu also carries Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Reduce By Half, Shift Left and Shift Right, which rework what is already drawn on it
Note — on the Grain Pitch and Panning grids a shift-drag sets a range rather than one value, and those two grids carry Reset Range in their own right-click menus as well
Menu — Load Sample 1 — reads a WAV file into the first of the sixteen sample slots, and Load Sample 2 through Load Sample 16 fill the rest
Menu — Load Directory — reads the WAV files of a folder into the sixteen sample slots
Menu — Clear Samples — empties all sixteen sample slots
GrainsOfWrath.notes: Thirty-one inputs, a reset input, two parameters and a third output are declared with no widget on the panel and are left untagged. The two V/OCT inputs match a volt per octave only at one volt either side of zero; past that the code adds the voltage to a rate multiplier rather than scaling exponentially.
